correctness.rationale: Reduction by nb=(n+1)a and nc=(n+1)b gives a nonnegative normal form; reducing first modulo n and then dividing after removal of jc determines the two bounded digits. For residue un+j, its quotient threshold is u−j+(n+1)ceil((2j−u)/n). Within a row of residues it decreases by one except for jumps of size n at j=floor(u/2)+1 and, precisely when u≤n−3, j=floor((n+u)/2)+1. At the boundary from u to u+1 the preceding threshold is at least u+2 and the next is u+1; multiples of a cannot start a gap block. Each positive jump supplies exactly n consecutive lifts giving the two disjoint progression families. The maximum and sum of the rectangle give the stated Frobenius number and genus. The coefficient of (1−z) times the membership generating function is a successive indicator difference, so each maximal gap block contributes exactly two changes, plus the constant coefficient counted separately. For n=2 there are four starts 1,5,7,11 and support nine. The separately authored reachability check /workspace/branches/2f35973e-7263-48b0-be6d-395a6258d6ef/independent_gap_check.py matched starts, genus, conductor and support for n=2..40; log independent_gap_check_chunks.txt. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed. The residue argument, not the finite test, proves the quantifiers.
